Shanaka to Dutt, OUT 
Castled! That'll do. Sri Lanka prevail in a nerve-jangling contest. Bangs it on a full length 
and it does enough off the seam to rip through the stumps. Sri Lanka's captain snares 
the final wicket and has a big broad smile on his face. They can breathe a sigh of relief 
but credit to Netherlands for giving Sri Lanka a run for their money. Once again, Sri 
Lanka's well-oiled potent bowling attack bailed them out of trouble and defended a low 
total successfully 
Aryan Dutt b Shanaka 7 (25b 0x4 0x6 26m) SR: 28 
CharithD: "Spare a thought for Edwards.. batting with tail, scoring nearly run a ball with 
only 28 ou of 68 scored via boundaries.. it isan absolute gem of an inning " 
Tahir: "Writing is on the wall for the full members after this fierce competition b/w the 
associates and low flying full members. SL gave lesson to full members in Asia cup 
specially Inda. I see one of the teams from this round in WC semi." 
Migara Kule: "Unless Scotland win all of their remaining matches, fair to say that SL are 
almost through given their healthier NRR" 
Ishan R: "Sri Lankan fans can breath easily now" 
Dhananjaya de Silva, Player of the Match: "It was a tough match, they fought hard from 
the start, had a good start and I was lucky to have batted well. My idea was to bat 
through till the fifty overs. Theekshana batted really well; I was just telling him to not get 
out, even Wanindu batted well. I would like to bat in the middle-order and it was good to 
spend some time in the middle. The boys are doing well in all three departments" 
Dasun Shanaka, Sri Lanka Captain: "It was a tough game as the score wasn not enough. 
We still managed to cross the line. We played some rash shots. We batted first in the 
last few games, so we knew the conditions. In a tournament like this, you might be 
down, but I am still taking it. We'll have to play according to the conditions in the first 
ten overs. (On Dhananjaya de Silva's innings) It's a masterclass innings, he deserved a 
hundred. Not many people can do that from that position. We knew we could defend 
with our bowling. Scott was on strike, I wanted to keep Theekshana for the other batter, 
that's why I bowled. (On Kumara's injury scare) Still assessing, we'll get to know after 
the match. I want to win all the coming matches." 
Scott Edwards, Netherlands Captain: "Yes, definitely, we're disappointed. At the halfway 
mark, we thought they were under-par. We had a good start. Credit to them, they bowled 
well in that little patch there and we couldn't get over the line. We bowled well 
throughout the whole innings. Dhananjaya batted exceptionally well, he didn't give us 
many chances. We were disappointing with the bat. A run-out like that or a great piece 
of fielding can change the game. We bat deep...we should have gotten over the line. I 
look at the field and see what it is (on playing sweep shots against Hasaranga and 
Theekshana). They are quality bowlers, you got to find a way to put pressure on them. 
Going into the game, we knew we had guys who can bat. All the way, I was confident. 
There was a bit of reverse at the end there and a bit of spin. I back those boys. We will 
go back and have a look at what we could have done better today. But yeah, in this 
whole tournament, you never know what's gonna happen. We'll do what we can in the 
next two two games" 
Edwards was middling the ball well and used the sweep shot to great effect but just 
didn't have enough support from the other end. Nevertheless, brilliant batting under 
tremendous pressure, he nearly got his team over the line. 
The spinners were on the money and didn't allow Sri Lanka to get off the hook. 
Theekshana and Hasaranga turned on the heat once again and showed their dexterity 
as the Netherlands started to run out of answers. Once Theekshana triggered the slide, 
Netherlands' resistance started to melt away even though the asking rate was never an 
issue. In hindsight, the Dutch team will be gutted with the result after doing everything 
right with the ball; the flurry of wickets they lost took the game away from them. Dilshan 
Madushanka made a mark straightaway with his lightning-fast face that hustled the 
opening batters; he flummoxed MP O'Dowd with a pitch-perfect yorker. 
Sri Lanka were in massive trouble after a scorching new-ball burst from Logan van 
Beek. But Dhananjaya de Silva batted with patience, soaked in pressure, showed 
maturity and made sure Sri Lanka get past 200. A word for Bas de Leede, whose blazing 
spell cleared the tail quickly and then later his virtuoso innings of 41 kept the 
Netherlands in the hunt. 
What a day of cricket it has been! The players gave their all, and we witnessed a tense 
contest. Until we meet again, stay passionate, stay connected, and keep loving the 
game. This is Rvel Zahid, saying goodbye on behalf of my fellow commentator 
Madushka Balasuriya and our scorer for this game K Vairavan.
